Empirical Research Plan ‑ Staple‐Grain Responses to Price and the U.S. Renewable Fuel Standard (RFS)

────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────
Method:  Multi-period, crop-level Difference-in-Differences (DiD) with an event-study (dynamic DiD) extension.

Rationale  
• The RFS created a plausibly exogenous, discrete and very large demand shock that fell almost exclusively on one crop—U.S. (and therefore world) corn—starting in marketing year 2005/06 and ramping up through 2010.  
• The other three major staples (rice, wheat, soybeans) faced the same macro, energy, and weather environment but were not directly mandated for fuel. They provide a natural counterfactual trend.  
• Because the mandates phase-in over several years, a dynamic event-study allows us to test pre-trends and to trace out the evolution of the treatment effect, strengthening causal interpretation.  
• Crop-by-year panel (4 crops × 50 years = 200 cells) gives enough observations to estimate flexible models while keeping the analysis at the level at which prices are observed (global futures markets).  

Secondary analyses  
• Triple-Diff (DDD): further interact with “high-U.S.-exposure” dummy (corn grown in the United States vs. outside) to rule out global shocks.  
• Instrumental Variables: use the mandate-driven ethanol blend requirement (billion gallons) as an instrument for corn demand in a simultaneous‐equations supply-and-demand system to retrieve structural elasticities; however, the core reduced-form answer to “How much did RFS raise world prices?” comes from DiD.

────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable  
Treated = 1 for crop = corn and year ≥ 2005 (baseline) or, in the dynamic specification, for leads/lags relative to 2005.

Control group  
Rice, wheat, and soybeans in all years + corn in the pre-period (1961-2004).

Treatment timing  
Event year = 2005 (Energy Policy Act). Robustness:  
• Alternative event year = 2007 (EISA, RFS2)  
• Continuous treatment: mandated ethanol gallons / world corn production (captures ramp-up 2005-2010).

No running variable; hence RDD is not applicable.

────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Parallel trends: absent the RFS, corn prices (and derived outcomes such as cropland) would have evolved like the weighted average of the three control crops.  
  Plausibility: Before 2005 the four price series moved closely; this will be tested formally in the event-study pre-period.

A2. No differential contemporaneous shocks: no other 2005-2010 shock uniquely affecting corn.  
  Plausibility: Other biofuel demand (biodiesel for soy) went in the opposite direction, making our estimate conservative. We will control for oil prices, global GDP growth, and weather shocks.

A3. SUTVA/no spillovers to controls: the mandate raises corn prices, which could spill over to substitutes (wheat, rice, soy).  
  Plausibility: Some spillover is expected; the DiD therefore recovers the *relative* price increase. We translate this into absolute effects with an elasticity matrix in a post-estimation step.

────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies
────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Oil-price boom (2005-08) could raise all crop prices, violating parallel trends.  
  Remedy: include log real crude-oil price × crop fixed effect; do robustness using synthetic-control weighting that forces controls to match pre-2005 oil sensitivity.

T2. Weather shocks (e.g., 2006 Australian drought) differentially hit wheat.  
  Remedy: include global (and U.S.) growing-season temperature & precipitation shocks; repeat analysis excluding 1–2 extreme-weather years.

T3. Endogenous storage/stock draw-down (low inventories raise prices).  
  Remedy: control for beginning-of-year stock-to-use ratios (FAO/USDA); perform IV specification instrumenting stocks with lagged global weather.

────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# Load packages
library(data.table)     # fast data wrangling
library(fixest)         # DiD / high-dim FE
library(ggplot2)        # figures
library(modelsummary)   # neat tables

# 1. Data -----------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- fread("staple_global_1961_2010.csv")  # each row: crop-year

# 2. Variable construction ------------------------------------------------
dat[, `:=`(
  treated      = (crop == "corn"),
  post2005     = (year >= 2005),
  mandate_gal  = ethanol_mandate_bgal,          # exogenous series
  log_price    = log(real_price_cpi),           # FAO/CBOT deflated
  log_prod     = log(global_production_kcal),
  log_area     = log(global_area_ha),
  oil_price    = log(real_oil_price),
  temp_dev     = gs_temp - mean(gs_temp),       # growing-season anomaly
  precip_dev   = gs_precip - mean(gs_precip)
)]

# 3. Main DiD specification ----------------------------------------------
# Equation:  y_ct = α_c + γ_t + β*(treated_c × post_t) + X_ct'δ + ε_ct
did_price <- feols(log_price ~ treated:post2005 + oil_price +
                     temp_dev + precip_dev | crop + year,
                   data = dat, vcov = ~crop)

# 4. Dynamic event-study --------------------------------------------------
# leads_lags takes −10…+10 relative to 2005
dat[, rel_year := year - 2005]
event_price <- feols(log_price ~ i(rel_year, treated, ref = -1) +
                       oil_price + temp_dev + precip_dev |
                       crop + year,
                     data = dat, vcov = ~crop)

# 5. Robustness: alternative event year (2007) ----------------------------
dat[, post2007 := (year >= 2007)]
did_price_alt <- feols(log_price ~ treated:post2007 + oil_price +
                         temp_dev + precip_dev | crop + year,
                       data = dat, vcov = ~crop)

# 6. Preview results ------------------------------------------------------
etable(did_price, event_price, did_price_alt)

# 7. Plot event-study -----------------------------------------------------
es <- coefplot(event_price, keep = "rel_year::treated")
ggplot(es, aes(x = as.numeric(term), y = estimate)) +
  geom_point() + geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, lty = 2) +
  labs(x = "Years since 2005", y = "Log-price effect (corn vs. controls)")
```

────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────
Economic theory predicts an outward shift in the corn demand schedule equal to roughly 5 % of the combined staple-calorie market. With world short-run supply elasticity ≈ 0.25 and demand elasticity ≈ –0.15, the formula ΔP/P ≈ ΔQ / (ε_s – ε_d) implies:

ΔP/P ≈ 0.05 / (0.25 – (-0.15)) ≈ 0.05 / 0.40 ≈ 12–13 %.

Because controls pick up part of the spillover, I expect the DiD estimate to show a relative corn‐price increase of about 10 % by 2010, peaking near 15 % in 2008. Translating into welfare, world consumer surplus for staple calories likely fell by roughly US $20–30 billion (NPV 2005-10). Cropland expanded ~2 % (≈ 12 Mha), with ∼3/5 outside the United States.

────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment
────────────────────────────────────────
C1: No differential pre-trends (parallel trends) …… 1  
C2: Exogenous treatment timing (policy driven) …… 1  
C3: No interference affecting controls ………………… 0 (some substitution likely)  
C4: Stable units & measurement across time ……… 1  
C5: No omitted crop-specific shocks post-2005 …… 0 (oil & China demand—partially controlled)

Total: 3 / 5 ⇒ acceptable but calls for extensive robustness (already planned).

────────────────────────────────────────
End of research plan
────────────────────────────────────────
